author: reek
body: A shadowed let must not leak out of its scope. The inner binding of v is bound inside the then-arm of the if, and the trailing `inner + v` reads the OUTER v, which is 2. The answer is 9.

author: reek
body: It is 13 today, because the emitter's locals table is flat per function: add-local prepends a binding and nothing ever pops it, so the inner v shadows the outer one for the rest of the function and the trailing read finds the inner slot, which still holds 6. The fixed point cannot see this - both stages agree on the wrong answer - and neither can ir-check, which asks whether a name is bound, not which binding it resolves to.
